title: The demo for my solo-built space 4X, Imperium, just went live on Steam
author: keaslenyt
selftext:
Been heads-down on this since March. Since the last announcement, I have done a full art refresh. The aliens are now more diverse and alien while also more consistent and faithful to the games art style, all planets, stars, asteroids and ship are now fully 3D. My workflow includes Claude Coe and GPT Astra, Tripo3D, as well as manual Blender and Photoshop work. Happy to answer any questions. :)  


About the game: It's a single-player 4X - colonize planets, design your ships piece by piece, and win through diplomacy or war against AI empires that scheme against each other too, not just you.

The demo drops you into a small galaxy with up to 3 AI opponents and three species to start with (Veylilith, Throk, Zyyth Azr), capped around year 1500 so you get a real early-to-mid game without spoiling the full run. Full game has 21 species, five hull classes, and a proper diplomacy system.

Only English for now, but Chinese, Russian, and Japanese localisation is in the pipeline already.

Free on Steam, no strings, but a wishlist would be appreciated ;)

comments.author: Ulnari
comments.body:
Thanks for the Mac build, but I encountered an issue (managed to run it in the end).

Claude's summary:  
The macOS demo build is failing Gatekeeper, and it's a packaging issue, not a signing one.

The .app bundle ships AppleDouble sidecar files inside it:

  Contents/.\_Info.plist

  Contents/.\_CodeResources

  Contents/.\_\_CodeSignature

  Contents/MacOS/.\_Imperium

  Contents/Resources/.\_Imperium.pck

  ...12 in total

These are the \`.\_\*\` files macOS creates when a file with extended attributes gets written to a filesystem that can't store them (exFAT, FAT32, SMB share, some zip paths). They're metadata only, no game content — but they're extra files inside a sealed bundle, so the signature no longer matches:

  $ codesign --verify --deep --verbose=4 [Imperium.app](http://Imperium.app)

  Imperium.app: a sealed resource is missing or invalid

  file added: .../Contents/MacOS/.\_Imperium

  file added: .../Contents/.\_Info.plist

  ...

Users get "Imperium.app is damaged and can't be opened" on first launch. The signature and notarization themselves are fine (Developer ID, ticket stapled) — it's purely the extra files.

replies.author: keaslenyt
replies.body: Thank you for the detailed message. I will address this urgently. :)
